name: BetterHelp
short_description: The world's largest online therapy platform connecting clients with licensed therapists via text, video, phone, and live chat. Self-pay subscription model, no insurance accepted.
long_description: BetterHelp is the world's largest online therapy platform, founded in 2013 and acquired by Teladoc Health in 2015 for approximately $4.5 million. The platform has grown exponentially and now serves over 2 million clients with a network of 30,000+ licensed therapists across all 50 states and internationally. BetterHelp operates on a self-pay subscription model (no insurance accepted), with clients paying weekly or monthly fees for unlimited messaging plus weekly live sessions. The platform offers therapy via text messaging, live chat, phone calls, and video sessions. Unlike platforms that accept insurance, BetterHelp's self-pay model means no credentialing delays or insurance billing complexity for therapists. Providers work as independent contractors with flexible schedules, setting their own hours and client load. BetterHelp's proprietary matching algorithm connects clients with therapists based on preferences, specialties, and availability. The platform handles all client acquisition, billing, and technical infrastructure. BetterHelp also operates specialized platforms including ReGain (couples therapy), Teen Counseling (teen therapy), Pride Counseling (LGBTQ+ focused), and Faithful Counseling (faith-based).
one_liner: World's largest online therapy platform (30,000+ therapists). Self-pay only. 17% pay fairness rating—tiered engagement-based compensation.

seo.title: BetterHelp for Therapists: Provider Jobs, Pay & Reviews | HeyPsych
seo.meta_description: BetterHelp therapist review: pay rates, requirements, and what it's like working for the world's largest online therapy platform. 30,000+ therapists, no insurance billing.

faqs.q: How much do BetterHelp therapists get paid?
faqs.a: BetterHelp uses a tiered engagement-based pay model. Therapists report $30-70 per engaged hour depending on tier, with effective rates often closer to $30-45/hour when factoring in messaging time. The 17% pay fairness rating on Comparably reflects widespread compensation concerns. Full-time therapists (25-35 hrs/week) report $50,000-$80,000 annually, but this varies significantly.

faqs.q: What is BetterHelp's pay fairness rating?
faqs.a: BetterHelp has a 17% pay fairness rating on Comparably, meaning only 17% of employees/contractors feel fairly compensated. This is among the lowest ratings for therapy platforms. For comparison, Talkspace rates 11%. Both are well below industry standards for mental health platforms.

faqs.q: What was the BetterHelp FTC settlement?
faqs.a: In 2023, BetterHelp paid $7.8 million to settle FTC charges that it shared sensitive user health data with Facebook and other advertisers despite privacy promises. The company denied wrongdoing but agreed to updated privacy practices. Some providers cite this as an ethical concern when choosing platforms.

faqs.q: What are the requirements to become a BetterHelp therapist?
faqs.a: BetterHelp requires licensed mental health professionals (LCSW, LMFT, LPC, PsyD, PhD) with at least 3 years post-licensure experience and 2,000+ clinical hours. You must be licensed in a US state, pass a background check, complete a video interview, and have reliable internet with a private workspace.

No, BetterHelp operates exclusively on a self-pay subscription model. Clients pay $60-90/week directly. This means no insurance credentialing or billing complexity for therapists, but also limits your client pool to those who can afford self-pay rates.

faqs.q: How does BetterHelp compare to Talkspace for therapists?
faqs.a: Both use engagement-based pay with low pay fairness ratings (BetterHelp 17%, Talkspace 11%). Both pioneered text therapy. BetterHelp is self-pay only (no insurance); Talkspace accepts some insurance. Talkspace had April 2025 bonus cuts. Neither lets you build an independent practice or take clients when you leave.
Yes, BetterHelp provides professional liability (malpractice) coverage for therapy conducted through the platform at no additional cost to therapists.
